strengths: Substantial practical efficiency improvements (60-90% speedup in post-extraction training time) consistently demonstrated across diverse datasets, backbones, and settings
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with thorough ablations, sensitivity analyses, and reproducibility (detailed pseudocode, training details, code availability promised)
Clear problem formulation of multicollinearity in representation-based CL with effective visualizations (Figure 3) showing progressive decorrelation through pipeline stages

Broad applicability across architectures (ViT, ResNet) and settings (batch, online, long sequences, severe domain shift) with well-integrated technical components (GCV adaptive regularization, Cholesky optimization)
Practical value for edge deployment avoiding model storage overhead compared to mixture-based approaches
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: each component (sparse random projection, top-k sparsification, ridge regression, streaming statistics) is established; main contribution is engineering their combination with incremental improvements

Loose biological motivation: paper acknowledges KC→MBON decorrelation evidence is 'inconclusive'; modeling via streaming ridge regression is significant abstraction; biological connection appears retrofitted rather than fundamentally inspiring algorithmic design

Unclear causal mechanism: multicollinearity shown to exist (Figure 3a) but not convincingly demonstrated as the main bottleneck addressed by method; improvements could stem from other factors (adaptive regularization, data normalization effects, sparse projection benefits)

Data normalization as confounding factor: Table 7 shows significant performance variation with architecture-specific normalization strategies; unclear if this normalization equally benefits all baseline methods, potentially explaining observed improvements

Incremental theoretical contributions: Theorem 4.1 applies standard results (Tao & Vu 2006); Theorem 4.2 makes strong assumptions (B.2, B.3) that may not hold after random projection, provides loose bounds, and lacks actionable guidance for hyperparameter selection

Inconsistent performance across settings: accuracy drops on CIFAR-100 (93.89% vs RanPAC's 94.21%); gains vary significantly by dataset (2-3% CIFAR-100 vs ~1% CUB); online CL shows smaller improvements than batch mode

Incomplete ablations: Figure 4 combines sparse projection and top-k without isolating individual contributions; missing ablation on adaptive GCV vs fixed regularization; no component-level contribution analysis beyond Table 4

Insufficient comparison with F-OAL: highly similar approach yet F-OAL competitive on CUB and VTAB without top-k operation; ResNet-50 degradation attributed to 'error accumulation' but lacks rigorous explanation for why sparse projection specifically helps
